request:
A world in the BAXTER-RAFVII sector, kept after Stephen Baxter — Raft.

The operations this world is built from:
- Alternative Gravity: a universe where gravity changes anatomy, architecture, and culture (cosmos, alteration).
- Alternative Fundamental Constants: a universe where different constants produce different chemistry and different stars (cosmos, substitution).

When we arrive: Under extreme gravity, bodies are short, architecture spreads horizontally, and the idea of jumping belongs to religion.

The central tension we want to continue: Vela saves a mine with antigravity and discovers that an engineering miracle instantaneously redistributes political authority

What the course asks of this world: Stephen Baxter — Raft; Greg Egan.

sourceText: Aster did not announce the night’s theme. She opened the BAXTER-RAFVII sector and let the children discover for themselves which of the world’s rules concerned them directly. Under extreme gravity, bodies are short, architecture spreads horizontally, and the idea of jumping belongs to religion. The memorial bore the name of Stephen Baxter — Raft precisely to keep the genealogy of the idea visible. Aster considered it indecent for a late civilization to treat the imagination of the past as anonymous ore: authors did not own the futures, but they deserved to remain on the map as points of intellectual origin. In the worlds of this period, a single physical deviation had to be followed all the way through. If gravity changed, so did walking, the house, the weapon, the metaphor, the frontier, and the price of a life saved. Orin perceived counterfactual costs as absences with weight. He did not confuse an unrealized branch with a victim, but he refused to let success rewrite rejected options as if they had been inevitable all along. At the center of the conflict was Rho, an administrator chosen precisely because they were not a specialist in the phenomenon that had reorganized the world. ‘The specialists tell me what can be done,’ 63 they said. ‘I have to answer who it may be done to.’ Kesh kept the distinction in his notes. The problem closed quickly around them: Vela saves a mine with antigravity and discovers that an engineering miracle instantaneously redistributes political authority. There was no clean option. Every intervention shifted the cost between persons, eras, or definitions of personhood; and refusing to intervene was itself a choice made by those who could leave. Kesh opened the analytical layer of the Table for a few seconds. The active cells were Cg — Alternative Gravity: gravity changes anatomy, architecture, and culture; Cf — Alternative Fundamental Constants: different constants produce different chemistry and different stars. Course references included Stephen Baxter — Raft; Greg Egan; hard SF. The rule was strict: naming a work did not substitute for an explanation. They had to identify the mechanism that could migrate into another story and the consequences that could not be copied without remainder. Orin broke the first consensus. ‘I do not want the perfect branch. I want us to know what we sacrificed in order to call it perfect.’ Tern answered without raising their voice: ‘Sometimes the ethical question is whether we are entitled to know enough to optimize.’ It was not a pedagogical quarrel. Over the last nights, the children’s differences had become incompatible political programs. Aster felt the Hunger precisely when an explanation closed too elegantly. A perfect theory reduced surprise, and surprise was the last symptom that something before her had not yet become part of her. 64 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS The children had noticed that their disagreement calmed her more than any extravagant universe did. Marae remained in the local body when the others opened their protections. The gesture cost her: she felt cold, pressure, and physiological delay at exactly the scale the inhabitants felt them. “Otherwise we risk confusing the fact that we survive with the claim that the situation is bearable,” she said after catching her breath. The night did not end in victory. The children learn that a physical constant produces values, metaphors, and institutions, not merely bodies. Aster recorded the decision in the world’s provenance register and, more importantly, allowed its inhabitants to contest it. For several eras she had been learning something that seems banal to lesser powers: technical reversibility is not the same as biographical reversibility. Tern remained a few seconds after the others. A very faint deviation repeated in the sector’s background noise, too coherent to be thermal and too useless to be a teaching signal. He did not tell Aster. It was the first thing he possessed solely by not sharing it. For the course, Kesh also linked the night to the COPYING operator. In the Table, periodicity did not mean that the same objects reappeared, but that the same operation — creates a second instance similar enough for continuity to become a problem — could recur across different families. Thus a copy of a body, a copy of a mind, a copy of a world, and a copy of a history were not the same phenomenon, but they shared a conceptual chemistry. 65 Vela introduced the propagation test: if you remove the speculative idea and nothing in the institutions, relationships, or vocabulary has to be rewritten, the idea has remained scenery. Kesh introduced the opposite test: if the idea seems to explain every detail, you have overcompressed the world. Between the two tests lay the region in which an element became fertile without becoming superstition. Marae added the refusal test. Who can say “no,” and what happens afterward? In universes with near-divine technology, that question often separated an instrument from a regime. A power that treats refusal as a data error can be benevolent in intention and totalitarian in structure. They left without an oral summary. Aster had abandoned the habit of closing every night with a thesis; some worlds were more honestly preserved as problems than as lessons. 66 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS
